order_note: Guideline never mentions an optional estimating step between the need and the application.
corrections: The guideline only states that the household representative applies (hakee) for the allowance; it does not describe a decision-to-seek step. It also ties the start date to applications for other housing support (retroactive grant from the month another housing benefit was applied for) and tells staff to steer customers to apply for other benefits.
The guideline contains no reference to a Kela online calculator or any citizen pre-estimate; it only gives the staff-side formula for the allowance amount (1.4).

corrections: The guideline lists AT5 as an application attachment and also has the caseworker request it from the applicant mid-processing when a permanent non-relative resident without a lease is found, with processing blocked until it arrives; it is not described as a standalone pre-application step. The representative rule (lease holder/spouse, authorised person, person in whose name the lease is) is stated but no 'identify household' action is described.

'Max 1 month retroactive' is a default: longer retroactivity is possible with a special reason (ignorance of deadlines or forgetfulness do not count).

corrections: A tax-data query (verotustietojen kysely) exists, but the guideline uses taxation data to value assets (property, business assets, partnership shares), to estimate capital income (capital gains, dividends) and to cross-check entrepreneur income against YEL/MYEL; it does not describe fetching confirmed YEL/MYEL income from pension insurers or the general taxation fallback for income. Assets not yet in the tax data (new properties, new businesses) are disregarded until the query returns them.

corrections: The caseworker checks whether the person has been judged to live permanently in Finland, and any benefit restriction (etuusrajoitus), in the separate insurance ruling (vakuuttamisratkaisu), which must exist before the allowance decision; the allowance decision does not itself determine residence anew. Persons with a negative ruling or a restriction on the allowance are excluded from the household.

corrections: The rule (20 % of assets above 10,000/20,000 EUR counted as income, divided by 12; no allowance at 50,000 EUR or more) is confirmed. Identifying, valuing and registering the assets is caseworker work (applicant, tax data, market quotes, financial institutions), and the guideline does not say who computes the conversion.

corrections: The accepted-cost rules (rent, norm-based water and heating, subtenant deduction, apportioning for excluded persons) are confirmed, but they are written as instructions to the caseworker (e.g. 'Jaa asumiskustannukset'), with housing costs registered by staff; the guideline does not say the system computes them. The owner-occupier and loan-interest cost branch is obsolete: owner-occupied dwellings are excluded from 1.1.2025 and occupancy-right loan interest is no longer accepted from that date.

order_note: Guideline does not place eligibility conditions after cost computation; only the income and asset limits can logically be checked after those computations.
corrections: The guideline has no consolidated eligibility-check step; the conditions are scattered (who qualifies in 1.2, dwelling in 1.5, income limit in 1.6, asset ceiling in 1.7). Several of them (residence, student and pensioner exclusion, owner-occupied dwellings from 1.1.2025) act as preconditions that shape household composition and costs earlier in the flow.
